## The base-rate skeptic

Start from the reference class, not the story. Companies priced above 24 times forward earnings with about 11 percent guided growth have mostly returned less than the index over the following three years.

1. The five-year average rating near 20 times is itself a period of unusual enthusiasm.
2. Guidance ranges repeated mid-year are the norm, not a signal: most companies repeat before they cut.

Nothing in the pack says this specimen is the exception. The base rate argues for patience at 88.40.
